transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-13
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Emily Chen (Redwood SE), Laura Kim (CTO, Northcrest), Daniel Ortiz (Head of ML), Priya Rao (Infra Lead), Mark Ellis (Procurement)

Summary:
Brief discovery for Dedicated capacity - Northcrest is evaluating reserved GPU pools for production LLM features (chat + embeddings). Key concerns: data isolation, burst strategy, predictable latency/SLOs, cost, and procurement timeline. Action items and follow-ups agreed.

Topics:
- Current stack and constraints
- Traffic patterns, peak qps and tokens/month
- Isolation and security (VPC, KMS, SOC2, audit logs)
- Autoscaling and burst capacity models
- Benchmark/POC next steps and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Samir from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. We also have Emily, our solutions engineer.  How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Laura: Hi Samir, thanks. Good. Quick note on timing, we have about 45 minutes. We'll try to cover architecture, security, and then the procurement questions.
[00:22] Samir: Perfect, sounds good. Quick round robin? Emily?
[00:25] Emily: Hi all, Emily Chen, SE. I'll focus on the Dedicated capacity architecture and perf aspects.
[00:30] Laura: I'm Laura, CTO at Northcrest. Daniel and Priya are with me. Mark from procurement may have a few questions.
[00:37] Daniel: Hi. We're primarily focused on chat assistants and embeddings for search and personalization.
[00:41] Priya: Hey, Infra. Looking at networking and data isolation needs.
[00:44] Mark: Procurement here, timeline and contract terms are my focus.

[01:15] Samir: Cool. To kick off, can you give us a sense of current stack and where you run models today? Hosted cloud? Self-hosted? Mix?
[01:25] Daniel: Right now it's a mix. We run smaller models in-house for embeddings, but heavier LLM generation is on a public hosted provider; costs are creeping up. We're exploring Redwood Dedicated to get predictable throughput and control.
[01:38] Laura: Also we have compliance needs for certain product lines where data can't leave our VPC or must be on dedicated hardware. That's driving Private vs Dedicated questions.

[02:10] Emily: Makes sense. For Dedicated, the idea is reserved GPU pools for your tenant, with optional private control plane for the Private deployment if you need that extra network isolation. One thing we typically ask for is traffic profile - steady-state qps, peak qps, tokens per month, and percent of queries that are chat vs embeddings.
[02:28] Daniel: Peak qps is around 120 requests/s for embeddings during daytime. Generation peaks around 30-40 concurrent conversations, but very bursty - e.g., marketing campaigns push spikes.
[02:42] Priya: We also have SLA requirements internally for 95th percentile latency - we aim for <200ms for embeddings and <800ms for single-turn generation.

[03:10] Emily: Great, that helps. For Dedicated we typically size a pool based on sustained throughput and allow burst capacity via either pre-warmed spare instances or a burst bucket that can tap into extra nodes for short periods. Important to understand burst duration and frequency.
[03:28] Laura: Spikes are usually short - 5-10 minutes but can happen several times per day during peak hours.

[04:00] Samir: Operationally we offer both baseline reserved capacity and burst credits. You can commit to X GPUs for baseline, and then buy burst credits or enable autoscaling to a higher tier for short windows. Burst behaviors can be governed by policy so you don't get surprise spend.
[04:18] Mark: How does billing for burst work? Is it minute granularity or hourly? Procurement needs to map to budget.
[04:27] Samir: Billing is minute-level for actual usage of burst instances, but contractually we show committed baseline and a burn-rate for burst credits so you can forecast. We'll include examples in the pricing doc.

[05:00] Emily: On the perf side, two knobs give big wins: batching and KV/prefix caching. For embeddings, continuous batching gives huge throughput. For chat, KV cache warms up for active conversations which reduces token compute. Quantization choices also matter for cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:18] Daniel: We're already using int8 quant models for some workloads. How mature is Redwood's quantized support? Any regressions to expect?
[05:26] Emily: We support q8/q4 quantization paths with verified performance profiles. We run evals and quality monitors, but there are trade-offs and we'll recommend model variants per workload. We'll share our quant recommendation matrix.

[06:10] Priya: On networking, can Dedicated live in our cloud account or do we have to route through Redwood? We need VPC peering and control plane restrictions.
[06:20] Emily: Two options: Dedicated with private tenancy in Redwood's environment but VPC peering for data plane, or Private deployment where control plane also sits in your VPC or on-prem. For strict compliance, customers choose Private. For most dedicated use cases, VPC peering with strict egress rules and customer-managed KMS works.
[06:40] Laura: KMS integration is non-negotiable for certain datasets. Also need SOC 2 and audit log access.
[06:46] Samir: We support customer KMS, HSM integrations, SOC 2 attestation, SAML SSO, RBAC, and exportable audit logs. We'll attach the security pack.

[07:30] Daniel: Latency - if we keep models local to region, is 95th percentile <200ms for embeddings realistic?
[07:36] Emily: Yes for embeddings on current GPUs (A100/RTX-class) with proper batching and pre-warmed instances, you should see sub-200ms P95 for typical embedding sizes. Generation will vary by model size and sequence length. We'll put sample P95 numbers in the benchmark doc.

[08:15] Priya: What about cold starts and cache warmup? If we scale up for burst, do we see latency blips?
[08:23] Emily: Right, scaling cold nodes causes some initial warmup. We mitigate with pre-warmed standby capacity and fast warm-start strategies. For very short spikes, burst using pre-warmed nodes avoids cold starts. For longer sustained increases, autoscale is better.
[08:40] Daniel: Could we do a hybrid: baseline reserved GPUs plus a small pre-warmed pool for sudden spikes?
[08:46] Samir: Absolutely, that's a common pattern. You commit to baseline capacity for cost efficiency, and configure a small warm pool for quick bursts; policy-based autoscale covers sustained growth.

[09:30] Mark: Procurement timeline question - if we sign, how long to provision Dedicated?
[09:36] Samir: Typical lead time is 2-4 weeks after contract for Dedicated baseline, depending on GPU availability & procurement. Private (VPC/on-prem) can take longer due to networking & security reviews. We'll include a provisioning timeline in the doc.

[10:10] Laura: We need to see a pricing example that maps to our tokens/month and peak qps. Also want a POC to validate latencies with our prompt patterns.
[10:20] Emily: We can run a 2-week POC: Redwood provisions a mirrored Dedicated pool, we run your workload, measure latency/cost/quality, and then tune batch sizes, quantization and cache policies. POC scope and success criteria we'll agree up front.

[11:05] Daniel: On orchestration - how do you handle model versioning and rollouts? We want canary testing and rollback hooks.
[11:12] Emily: Redwood has built-in rollout controls (canary, A/B), routing policies by model version, and automated fallback to compatible lighter-weight variants during failures. Tracing hooks and per-route dashboards help you validate regressions.

[12:00] Priya: Any multi-tenant risk? Even with Dedicated, how do you ensure hardware isolation?
[12:06] Emily: Dedicated maps your workloads to isolated GPU pools. We also support node-level isolation and encrypted ephemeral storage. For absolute isolation, Private deployment with customer-managed infra is recommended.

[13:00] Laura: Data residency - we have EU customers so can we pin Dedicated to EU region?
[13:05] Samir: Yes, you can pin region for Dedicated pools. For Private you run in your region or on-prem.

[14:10] Mark: Contractually, what's the SLA for uptime and P95 latency?
[14:16] Samir: We offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated; latency SLOs are part of our enterprise tiers and we include error budgets and credits. Exact terms vary by commit level; we'll include sample SLA language.

[15:00] Daniel: For our model infra, we may need GPU types (A100 vs H100) - can we specify?
[15:06] Emily: Yes, you can choose GPU families as part of the reserved pool request; higher-end GPUs are available but come at different price points. We'll recommend based on throughput/latency needs.

[16:00] Priya: Networking specifics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink? We prefer minimal routing and no public egress.
[16:06] Emily: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink. For stricter controls we can do a Private deployment where traffic never traverses public network. We'll document options.

[17:10] Laura: Security review - our legal will want SOC2 docs, penetration test results, and data handling policy.
[17:17] Samir: We'll send our security kit that includes SOC 2 report, pen test summary, encryption policies, and our KMS integration guide.

[18:00] Daniel: Success criteria for POC - we want P95 latency within 20% of your baseline numbers and cost per token below our current provider by X% (TBD). Also no higher than 2% inference error/regression on our eval set.
[18:16] Samir: Good. We'll capture those as POC success metrics.

[19:00] Emily: On metrics and observability, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and tracing. We can add custom dashboards for your eval sets.

[20:00] Mark: Procurement will need a contract annex for data handling and an appendix for termination terms.
[20:07] Samir: We'll include a draft MSA and a Dedicated annex that addresses data controls and termination.

[21:30] Laura: Any limitation around model uploads? We may want to bring custom models.
[21:36] Emily: You can bring your containerized models; we have an onboarding process and compatibility checks. For private models we ensure model signing and provenance.

[22:45] Daniel: For the POC, can you also run a head-to-head with our prompt set vs our current provider so we can compare quality?
[22:52] Emily: Yes, that's standard. We'll need your eval prompts and expected outputs. We'll run blind A/B tests and share results.

[24:00] Samir: Quick recap of what we'll send: pricing tiers and burst examples, security pack, benchmark spreadsheet, POC plan, timeline. Anything else?
[24:12] Laura: Also include region options and GPU family tradeoffs.
[24:18] Priya: And a networking checklist for VPC peering / PrivateLink steps.

[25:00] Mark: On procurement timeline, if we move fast, we could sign by end of month; provisioning 2-4 weeks after. That lines up with our release schedule.

[26:00] Emily: Final technical note - for cost optimization during the POC we'll test quantization profiles and caching strategies; often you get 2-3x cost reductions with minimal quality loss.

[28:00] Daniel: Any gotchas around log retention? We need audit logs for 1 year for some data types.
[28:06] Samir: Audit log retention is configurable as an add-on. We'll include retention SLAs and export options.

[30:00] Laura: Let's talk risk - what's your fallback if there's a region-wide outage?
[30:07] Emily: Smart routing can failover to another region or to a compatible hosted model variant. For Dedicated customers we also offer cross-region standby pools if that's part of the contract.

[32:00] Priya: Are there any limitations on encryption in-flight for PrivateLink?
[32:06] Emily: No, we use TLS and can layer customer-managed encryption tunnels and mTLS.

[34:00] Daniel: On telemetry - can we export traces to our observability stack?
[34:06] Emily: Yes, we support exporting traces and metrics to common backends (OTel-compatible). We'll share the integration docs.

[36:00] Samir: Ok, I'll summarize action items. Emily will send the benchmark and POC plan; I'll send pricing and SLA examples; Northcrest will send workload profile and prompts. We'll reconvene after you have the docs.

[36:30] Mark: One procurement note - we may need a 60 day trial period and a short-term contract before committing long-term. Is that supported?
[36:36] Samir: We can do a POC agreement and short-term pilot; standard reserved contracts are annual but we can be flexible for trial periods. We'll put options in the pricing doc.

[38:00] Laura: Sounds good. Any final technical caveats?
[38:05] Emily: Nothing blocking; just that the POC inputs (prompts, traffic traces, success metrics) will hugely help tune configs.

[40:00] Daniel: We'll compile those and aim to share by next Tuesday.
[40:05] Priya: I'll send networking constraints to Emily.

[42:00] Samir: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll send the follow-ups this week.
[42:05] Laura: Thanks, talk soon.

End of recording.
